name: CallRail
summary: Call tracking and attribution: which campaigns, keywords and ads produce phone calls and form leads. It is an attribution layer, not a phone system or CRM.
best_for: marketers and agencies that need to prove which campaigns, keywords and ads drive phone calls and form leads, with recordings and multi-touch attribution
skip_if: you don't run enough paid marketing to need call-level attribution, or your call volume would push overages past the value of the insight
honest_knock: The headline price is a floor, not a ceiling: the included minutes, numbers and SMS are modest, so an active campaign quickly hits metered overages that meaningfully lift the bill. It's also specifically an attribution tool: it proves which marketing drives calls and leads, but it isn't a phone system or CRM, so you add it alongside those, not instead of them.

pricing.entry_price_terms: a month (plus usage), or $50 a month billed yearly
pricing.notes: Four plans, read on callrail.com/pricing on 13 October 2026 in a live browser, each 'plus additional usage': Lead Tracking $55 a month, Lead Tracking Complete $105, Lead Conversion $165 and Lead Conversion Complete $215; on yearly billing the same four read $50, $95, $150 and $195 a month (the page states 'Save up to 10% with a yearly plan'). Every plan includes 5 local numbers, 250 local minutes and 25 text messages a month (texting only after the trial); the Complete plans add 1,000 form submissions. Usage past the allowance: extra local numbers $3 each, local minutes $0.06, toll-free numbers $5, toll-free minutes $0.08, texts $0.03, form submissions $0.02. API access is in every plan, free to 1,500 calls a month, then $80 a month (1,501-12,000) or $200 (12,001-300,000). Voice Assist (the AI answering agent) starts at $95 a month on top of Lead Tracking, plus $1 a call after 50 calls over 15 seconds. Users are unlimited on every plan. 14-day free trial, no card. When we signed up on 18 November 2026, the first phone verification did not accept a Dutch mobile number and sent no code; on a later attempt the account opened.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session opened the tracking number window of CallRail in a trial account that we created. In about 38 seconds and 4 steps it reached Number routing, where it stopped: the area code 212 gave No numbers available for that area code., the area code 415 gave a suggested number, and none of these steps showed a price, a card field or a phone verification. The button Activate tracking number stayed grey until a forwarding number is entered, and nothing was chosen or activated. After that the account showed Account pending, because unusual activity was detected during sign-up and the account was in review, so the dashboard, reports and sources were not seen. The pricing page shows $50, $95, $150 and $195 per month with a yearly plan, plus additional usage, a 14-day trial without a card to start, and $0.09 for a toll-free minute, where the dossier said $0.08; this is recorded as an update dated 18 Nov 2026. No payment screen was seen and cancelling was not tried. Account and start: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in his browser on 18 Nov 2026. The dossier name is CallRail and the review is on MSS (mss/callrail-review.html). The interface was already in English. The dossier already holds the buyer fact about the verification at sign-up; it was not repeated and not changed in this test. Audience: the dossier groups are marketers spending on ads that drive phone calls, busy small businesses with a tight call budget, and sales teams that need a phone system or CRM; the test followed the pain I don't know which ad brings in the phone calls. Number screen: the window Create tracking number was opened at 19:15:51 and the test stopped at 19:16:29, about 38 seconds and 4 steps. Step 1: Where will you display this tracking number? (On my website or Somewhere else). Step 2: Where do you want to use your tracking number? with a list of places (Google Ads Assets, Google My Business, Facebook, Instagram, Microsoft ads, Print ad, Google Local Services Ads, Yelp, Angi, Thumbtack, Home Advisor, LinkedIn and TikTok); Google Ads Assets was chosen. Step 3, Number setup: the switch Local / Toll-free, a field for a city or area code and a Number name (prefilled with Google Ads Assets). The area code 212 gave No numbers available for that area code.; the area code 415 gave a suggested number (Your new tracking number!) with the buttons Copy and Regenerate and the line Area code local to California. The number was only a suggestion and was not chosen. Step 4, Number routing (where the test stopped): Forward to phone number (Search or enter a number) or Use Call flow; Activate call recording is ticked by default with the message This call may be recorded and shared with third-party providers.; Activate whisper message; Message routing (marked New!); the button Activate tracking number stays grey until a forwarding number is entered. Nothing was entered and nothing was activated. No price, no card field and no phone verification was shown in any of these steps. Whether a phone verification is asked when a number is activated was not seen, because the button stayed grey. Blocked: after the window app.callrail.com led to Account Status: Welcome! We're waiting for someone to approve your trial. and Account pending. We detected unusual activity on this account during the sign-up process. We are reviewing your account for approval and may contact you for more information. The dashboard, the reports and the sources list were therefore not seen: the dashboard address and the analytics pages gave a 404 or the same pending page. Billing only said that past invoices would show there. Because of this the whole account was locked and no empty reports or sources could be judged. Plans up to the payment: Read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026 on the public pricing page (callrail.com/pricing, yearly switch on, Save up to 10% with a yearly plan): Lead Tracking $50/mo, Lead Tracking Complete $95/mo, Lead Conversion $150/mo and Lead Conversion Complete $195/mo, each plus additional usage. The dossier gives the monthly amounts $55, $105, $165 and $215; those were not read again on the monthly switch. Included: 5 local numbers and 250 local minutes (and 25 texts, Available after trial). Extra usage on the page: local numbers $3, local minutes $0.06, toll-free numbers $5 and toll-free minutes $0.09. The dossier says $0.08 for a toll-free minute: this is a change at the vendor, recorded as an update dated 18 Nov 2026 and not as a correction of the dossier. Trial: Every account starts with a 14-day free trial. We don't require a credit card to get started, and we won't bill you until your trial is over. CallRail is available in the United States, Canada, the UK and Australia. Inside the app the number steps showed no price and asked for no card and no phone verification, and Billing only said that past invoices would show there; no payment screen was seen. No plan was chosen and nothing was bought. Cancelling: not tested; the account was in review and Account details was not opened. Not tested: choosing or activating a number, the real cost of a number (the flow showed no price; only the pricing page gives $3 for an extra local number), the Toll-free tab, the call flow, the dashboard, reports, the sources list, usage alerts, a payment screen and cancelling. Clean up (still so): the account and the test data stay; nothing was created or activated, only an area code (212, then 415) was typed in the form; the own tab was closed.
exit_test.awkward: The account was held for review right after sign-up (unusual activity was detected), so the product itself could not be seen. The number steps show no price at all; the cost of an extra number is only on the pricing page. The button Activate tracking number stays grey until a forwarding number is entered. Call recording is ticked by default. The area code 212 gave no numbers.

The dashboard, reports and the sources list, which were locked while the account was in review.

Can a customer cancel at any time, and what happens to an annual plan that is cancelled mid-term?
Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
